turns.response:
Hostile validation verdict, admin PWA source candidate 437c501c58c7dfa96ee576f445d225f2dd62a0bd, gate admin-pwa-source-round1 (staging readiness only).

OverallVerdict DISAGREE. Accuracy 92. Completeness 88. Both are below 98, and surfaces 1, 2 and 3 each have a FAIL.

What holds: the security core is sound and well evidenced. The GitHub provider accepts only numeric id 16146732 with login sharpninja through S256 PKCE and state, and keeps no provider tokens. Guest and admin realms are separated by a hash namespace, and copied tokens fail both ways in real PostgreSQL. Public OpenAI, delegation and community routes are closed. The admin worker caches only static public files and passes HTTP errors through. Legacy retirement is narrowly scoped, navigation races are guarded, card whitespace meets 20px and 32px, and the presence fix is correct. All five TRX files match the request hashes and their native JUnit case by case, with 0 failed and 0 skipped, and all 60 unit files are present.

Why DISAGREE:
F1 (high, product): the verified GitHub owner profile is created as a public member and published on the public leaderboard and landing projection, with no opt-out. This contradicts DEC-11 and the guest-only public surface. The 19:32 PostgreSQL run surfaced it as an extra public row, and it was resolved by test cleanup, not product analysis.
F2 (medium, process): there is no documented BDPv4 green mock gate or chronological receipt for this slice. This needs an operator decision.
F3 (medium, traceability): GA-09 and GA-05/06/07 are not carried by any TR or TEST criterion, and GA/PWA rules are duplicated under second IDs.
F4 and F5 (low, evidence): the adapter validation is not reproducible, and three pwa.spec.ts cases were not rerun on committed bytes.
F6 to F8 are informational (QBrain read-time timestamps triaged, non-unique case names, reviewer effort and hooks not runtime-verified).

Not claimed and still pending: live GitHub consent, standalone phone cookie continuity, physical OS installation, hosted deployment, and GitHub App registration (class-2 operation, UNKNOWN).

actions.description: Wrote final verdict JSON receipt (review receipt only).
Wrote reviewer scripts and QBrain readback receipts (review audit only).

F1 [high/product-implementation] GitHub owner admin profile is published on the public leaderboard with no opt-out. Judgment: IdentityService.profile sets publicLeaderboard true for member kind (identity.ts:100). completeLogin creates the owner as member (identity.ts:221-227). wordpairs_public_profiles returns id and alias for every public_leaderboard profile with no wins or kind filter (002_public_reads.sql:22-24). The admin UI hides ProfilePreferences (identity-panel.tsx:210) and /api/profile uses the guest-only service, so the owner cannot opt out. The full PostgreSQL run at 19:32 failed TR-30 with exactly one extra public row (a bare runtime UUID, unlike test-local admin- ids), and the next green run followed test cleanup changes; no product analysis was recorded (inference on the row identity). Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC: GA-10 (new, or strengthen GA-03): The verified GitHub owner profile is created non-public and never appears in public leaderboard, landing or room-discovery projections; the public surface lists guest profiles only. Proposed tests: Unit tests/application/identity.test.ts: admin IdentityService completeLogin passes a member draft with publicLeaderboard false (negative control: true is rejected by the assertion). | PostgreSQL tests/integration/admin.integration.ts: after the owner callback, wordpairs_public_profiles and the landing route exclude owner.profile.id, without relying on cleanup order. | Browser: after an admin fixture session, the public landing/community board shows no member alias. Operator decision: Whether legacy member-kind profiles from the retired OpenAI flow should also be hidden from public projections in this guest-only release.

F2 [medium/process] No documented BDPv4 green mock gate or chronological receipts for this slice. Judgment: BDPv4 steps 4 and 7 require a documented green mock gate before production implementation and retained receipts proving order. The self-review states no such receipt is reconstructed; retained runs begin at 19:05 against implementation. This is a missing-receipt finding, not an FR-timestamp inference. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC: Operator decision required: accept a recorded process exception for this slice, or require a retroactive mock-gate evidence package before staging. Proposed tests:  Operator decision: Accept documented exception or require remediation.

F3 [medium/requirements-traceability] GA-05/06/07/09 not carried by any TR or TEST criterion; duplicate GA/PWA rules. Judgment: GA-09 has tests (tests/browser/pwa.spec.ts:118, tests/web/pwa-support.test.ts:139) but no TR/TEST record carries it. GA-06 is verbatim PWA-09; GA-05 and GA-07 restate PWA-01/03 and PWA-06/07. Two IDs for one rule invite drift. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC: Add GA-09 to a TEST record (TEST-ADMINUI-136 or a new TEST) with the 390x844/1440x900 geometry case; either map GA-05/06/07 onto TEST-PWAINSTALL-137/TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138 criteria or replace them with references to PWA-01/03/06/07/09. Proposed tests: Name tests/browser/pwa.spec.ts:118 and tests/web/pwa-support.test.ts:139 as the GA-09 cases in the TEST record. Operator decision:

F4 [low/evidence] Adapter fixture validation is a bare summary. Judgment: trx-adapter-validation.json records counts and the adapter hash only; no fixture inputs, harness or output are retained. This review compensated with a full TRX-to-JUnit cross-check of all five reports. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC: Retain the adapter validation harness, its three outcome fixtures, two negative-control inputs and the command output. Proposed tests: Pester or script test: Passed/Failed/NotExecuted fixtures convert exactly; empty report rejected; -WhatIf writes nothing. Operator decision:

F5 [low/evidence] pwa.spec.ts edited after the full browser run. Judgment: Only the card case was rerun on committed bytes. The other three pwa.spec.ts cases at committed bytes have no post-edit run, and the pre-edit bytes are not retained to prove the edit was confined to the card case. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC: Supply a run of all four pwa.spec.ts cases on the committed bytes, or the retained pre-edit diff. Proposed tests: npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts tests/browser/pwa.spec.ts (run by the implementer, supplied as TRX plus JUnit). Operator decision:

F6 [info/mcp-server] QBrain reads return read-time createdAt/updatedAt. Judgment: getFr/getTr/getTest/listMappings returned timestamps equal to the read time. Filed as triage-report-618a93a51dd54d92b620dba566f21bfb (group triage-group-55457f6e1613d9ae). Confirms FR timestamps cannot support chronology. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC:  Proposed tests:  Operator decision:

F7 [info/evidence] Non-unique it.each case names. Judgment: Three it.each groups emit identical names (github-admin.test.ts token endpoint x3, malformed transaction x3; hosted-sbom x2), so per-case TRX rows cannot be told apart by name. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC:  Proposed tests: Add %s or $index interpolation to those titles. Operator decision:

F8 [info/reviewer-runtime] Reviewer effort and hook enforcement not runtime-verified. Judgment: Model claude-opus-5-5 verified from the stream init event (response.jsonl line 7). Effort high is launcher-attested only; init reports per_turn_effort_active true without a value. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT was not set for this source plugin, so hook enforcement is reported unverified; the hook-announced turn req-20261029T005811Z-prompt-88ee was absent from this plugin workspace cache, so a dedicated review turn was opened. Consequence: blocks AGREE; proposed AC:  Proposed tests:  Operator decision:

OverallVerdict DISAGREE; accuracy 92; completeness 88; PASS 31 FAIL 4 UNKNOWN 3. Scores below 98 and FAILs on surfaces 1-3 require DISAGREE; candidate is not ready for staging until F1 is fixed and F2/F3 decided.
